classes.name: Loop diuretics
classes.description: Loop diuretics: furosemide (Lasix; tablets, oral solution; Furoscix subcutaneous on-body infusor and Lasix ONYU subcutaneous, alternatives only, never the pick), torsemide (generic; Soaanz), bumetanide (Bumex), ethacrynic acid (Edecrin; for sulfa allergy). Not thiazides.
classes.plainDescription: A strong water pill that removes extra fluid, for heart failure, kidney and liver disease and swelling.

preferredAgent.sig: Edema: 20 to 80 mg by mouth as a single dose; repeat or raise by 20 or 40 mg no sooner than 6 to 8 hours later until the response is right (label). Check potassium.
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill in the morning. Your dose may be adjusted to how much fluid you lose.

records.verificationNote: Read from the Anthem 2026 Select Drug List (four tier) text layer in layout mode; tier and Notes (PA/ST/QL) read on the same row. Legend: PA=prior authorization, ST=step therapy, QL=quantity limit, BE=benefit exclusion. The list prints no strengths for most generics. Loop diuretic rows on p. 51. Furosemide tablet, torsemide and bumetanide are Tier 1; ethacrynic acid Tier 2; none carries PA/ST/QL. Furoscix and Soaanz are absent from the complete list. Lasix and Bumex brands are not separate lines. [Sonnet check 2026-11-06: each nonformulary brand re-searched across all 80 pages (case-insensitive, whitespace/hyphen-stripped): confirmed absent; page-2 completeness line is circular (complete listing of drugs on the list), p. 3 says a drug not on the list may be paid at full cost, so the nonformulary calls are reasonable but worth a human glance.]
